<reason>A better defended the actual decision rule: mandatory pre-release evaluation, conservative thresholds, and withholding dangerous weights. A directly answered the enforcement and concrete-threshold questions. B established a serious irreversibility concern, but repeatedly attacked post-release intervention despite A's explicit preventive safeguards. Crucially, B supplied neither workable affirmative-approval criteria nor a sufficient justification for excluding advanced models without demonstrated severe misuse capability.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A turned B's testing objection against B's own proposal: affirmative approval still relies on imperfect hostile testing, unless its safety burden effectively prohibits advanced openness indefinitely. B's closing repeated the consequences of irreversible error without resolving that dilemma or adequately weighing unnecessary exclusion.</best_rebuttal>
